events.text:
Dear beneficiary,
We write on behalf of an estate that has named you. There is nothing for you to pay. Enclosed are a key, a deed to a small island, and a personal letter left for you. Please read the letter before you decide anything. If you choose to visit, a boat will be arranged. We regret that we are unable to answer questions about the estate.
New Life Inheritance
events.cause: Scene one, letter one: a plain envelope franked in a quay town, with a key and a deed folded in; formal and dull.

events.text:
Dear you,
I am sorry we never met. I would have liked to. Somehow it was always easier to send something than to turn up. So I helped from a distance, in small ways you may not have noticed.
I am leaving you an island. It is not much, but it is yours, and it is quiet. There is work to do there, and I think you will be good at it. Take your time.
Whatever you make of it will be right.
With love, from a distance.
events.cause: Scene one, letter two: a handwritten page in the same envelope, with the small plain mark under the last line.

events.text: A small flat, rain on the glass. Two letters, a key and a deed lie on the table beside a cold cup. Nothing to pay. You pack one bag.
events.cause: Card scene one: grey-brown light, rain on the glass, the letters, the key and an empty bag on the bed.

choices.label: Pack a tin of seeds
Pack a book of tide tables
Pack a small lamp

events.text: Wet pavements, shut shops, a loom hum from a mill that has not stopped. A woman sweeps her step in the rain and nods to you.
events.cause: Card scene two: sodium light on puddles; a kind nod, nothing more.

choices.label: Leave your last coins in the tin by the shuttered shop
Read the notice taped in a window
Walk on, hood up

events.text: A small, dull office. A clerk reads the papers aloud without looking up. An estate has named you: a deed, a key, a sum. The clerk says only that the office is unable to answer questions about it. A different name is signed on every page.
events.cause: Card scene three: a desk, a coat on a hook by the door, a brass key in a paper fold, signatures seen from above as marks, no face.

choices.label: Sign where it says
Ask to read it twice
Ask for a copy to keep, and sign after

events.text: A small station, a late train, steam on the glass. A board lists parcels held back for a week. Nobody seems alarmed.
events.cause: Card scene four: wet platform, a chalk board of delays, one lamp swinging.

choices.label: Hold the door for a woman with a pram
Study the board of delays
Sit by the window and watch the rain

events.text: The quay at the end of the line. A small boat, engine low. You step aboard with your bag and the key. The grey slides off the water and teal and gold come in.
events.cause: Card scene five: the palette flips from grey-brown to teal and gold as the boat leaves the wall; the town shrinks.

choices.label: Look back at the town
Look ahead at the sea
Turn the brass key over in your hand

events.text: This island is yours. So is what is in the ledger. Spend it slowly. Parcels will come by boat. If something looks old, it is probably still useful. You do not need to understand why.
events.cause: The crate above the tideline opens; paper letter, plain stamp, brass key; the ledger card unrolls.
events.source: beat 1 pattern (Mysterious Island): a crate nobody ordered

events.text: You can make this a place for people to visit. You can make it a place for wildlife. You can make it somewhere to live quietly. Or you can do all three badly. None of it is wrong.
events.cause: A second crate lands at the jetty with the evening tender; the build menu unfolds with five things.

events.text: A coat hangs on a hook inside the hut door. It is dry and brushed, though the roof leaks. The pockets hold nothing but a worn pencil.
events.cause: Tap the hut door: a coat on a hook, dry, with one pencil in the left pocket.
events.source: beat 2 pattern (Mysterious Island): a tool left behind

events.text: A chair stands at the hut window, turned to face the lamp on the headland. The seat is clean. The tide table on the wall is marked in pencil, with a tick against some of the low waters.
events.cause: Camera rests on the window chair; the pencil ticks line up with the Hoard windows on the tide card.

events.text: A shelf holds a row of plain envelopes, never opened, each with the small mark in the corner. Forty or so, one for each month. They are addressed to the island, not to you.
events.cause: The player opens the hut shutter: a shelf of cream envelopes; a count appears on the notebook.

events.text: The brass key turns in a small drawer under the table. Inside: a tide book, a pencil stub, and some papers with the plain mark where a signature should be.
events.cause: The player turns the key in the table drawer; the papers are laid on the table and a stamp is logged in the notebook.

events.text: Behind the hut stove, a hand saw, still oiled and wrapped in cloth. The teeth are sharp. It was left for someone to find.
events.cause: A cloth bundle behind the stove; the player unwraps a saw; a plank on the bench is cut and added to the heap.
events.source: beat 2 (Mysterious Island): a tool left behind

events.text: Five small cairns march out along the west skerry into the water. They stand on the sand that dries at low tide. Nobody told you how they got there.
events.cause: Camera pans west at dawn: a line of five stone piles runs from the skerry to the sea.

events.text: The glass falls all morning. By noon the sea is up on the beach. When it drops, the wrack line is heaped with timber, tins and rope. The old carriers are already working it.
events.cause: A tidal eddy and a surge push 24 heaps onto the wrack line; robots and the player carry from them; the hulk lies near the camp.
events.source: beat 4 (Robinson Crusoe): salvage before the next tide

events.text: The sea gives and takes. What it leaves is not rubbish, only things that have not found a use yet. The old carriers know the shore. Let them work.
events.cause: A crate on the next morning's tender; a paper panel opens.

events.text: At the lowest tide the old carriers cross the drying bar one by one, past the cairns. On the far island, sorted heaps wait in rows. Whoever sorted them did it with care.
events.cause: At the first low under -0.74 m the robots wade the wet bar; the player follows with a lantern and finds the depot terrace.
events.source: beat 1 pattern (Mysterious Island): a hidden stock

events.text: On the side of the biggest heap, a crate with the small plain mark. Nothing else on it. It is shut, and it is lightly oiled.
events.cause: The player brushes sand from a crate at the depot; the mark shows; the notebook adds a stamp.

events.text: You carry planks and rope from the sorted heaps to the bar with a robot at the other end of the load. The bar closes behind you with a soft hiss of tide.
events.cause: The player and a hauler robot carry a long beam between them across the bar; stock rises when it reaches the yard heap.

events.text: Under the green ridge, a thin spring runs from a cleft into a stone trough. The trough has been swept clean. You fill a barrel and row home.
events.cause: The player rows to the woods (about 80 s), fills barrels at the trough; the barrel icon rises as the barrels are lifted on the tender.

events.text: At a low spring tide the sill to the woods dries for an hour. The carriers haul a day of cut timber across it, one load at a time, while you hold the lantern end.
events.cause: Robots cross the sill in the 60 to 90 minute window; each load is carried to the yard heap, the player carries one end of the long ones.

events.text: From the lamp knoll, grey specks on the far ledges move and slide into the water. They are seals. They keep their distance, and so should you.
events.cause: At night two the lamp beam shows the seal ledges as specks; the notebook adds a tally.

events.text: Small black-and-white birds with bright bills whirr past the knoll and drop into the turf of the far rock. The spring has come.
events.cause: A scatter of puffins arrives at the seal island turf; the bird tally on the hide slate rises.

events.text: A gull walks off with a whole loaf from the table while you are looking at the sea. It sits on the roof and eats, and keeps an eye on you.
events.cause: A herring gull lands on the yard table, lifts the loaf, flies to the hut roof.

events.text: Fog sits on the sound all morning. The horn sounds, then nothing. The tender lies off and does not land until the evening.
events.cause: The horn sounds from the fog; the delivery marker slides a day; the tender waits off the jetty.

events.text: One carrier has stopped on the low sand, its light amber. The tide is turning. You will have to go and free it, and a second carrier will pull.
events.cause: A robot sits stopped in wet sand; the status light is amber; its tracks are filling.

events.text: You wedge a plank under the tracks and the second carrier tows on its rope. The first one jerks, clears the sand and rolls on. No one is hurt, only late.
events.cause: The player lays the plank, a second robot tows on a rope, the stuck robot's light goes green.

events.text: At dusk a carrier stops short of the post, its light dim. You push it the last few metres on the plank rollers. It charges all night.
events.cause: A robot with a dim light stops 10 m from the post; the player and another robot push it onto the plate.

events.text: After the storm a small boat grounds on the beach. A cold traveller sits in it, wrapped in a blanket. You give a meal and a bed and ask nothing. In the morning the boat is gone.
events.cause: A boat lies on the sand after the storm; a figure under a blanket by your fire; one more mark on the guest slate; later the boat is gone.
events.source: beat 13 (New Atlantis): strangers cared for without questions

events.text: Someone will arrive who did not plan to. Be kind first. The rest can be worked out later.
events.cause: A crate at the jetty the morning after the first visitor; the paper panel opens.

events.text: The evenings are long now. At ten the sky is still pale and the sea lies flat. The carriers work late, and the lamp is lit only when the stars are.
events.cause: Dusk comes late on the sky clock; robots stay out until 21:30; the lamp sprite stays dark until stars show.

events.text: A dry fortnight. The barrel shows a hand's width of water. You carry buckets from the woods spring by boat, and the garden drinks.
events.cause: The barrel water mark falls week by week; the player and a robot carry buckets from the tender.

events.text: The long dry spell comes, but the cistern holds. You open the tap and the water runs clear. The garden is green when the hill is brown.
events.cause: The cistern level bar falls slowly; the tap flows; the garden beds stay dark.

events.text: A small boat lands two guests for the day. They walk the strand, buy tea, take photographs of the lamp, and leave before the tide turns. They are only counted.
events.cause: A boat lands at the jetty, two figures walk, the guest slate gets two marks, the cash line rises when the tea is paid for.

events.text: Round-headed seal pups lie on the ledge in the long light. Their mothers watch the water. You stop the engine a long way off and let the tender drift.
events.cause: The player cuts the engine at 30 m; seals stay up; the tally on the slate rises by eight.

events.text: Gannets fold and fall into a silver patch of water. Dolphins follow. For an hour the sound is alive. You land three fat herring on a line.
events.cause: A shoal darkens the water off the lee shore; gannets dive; the line comes up with fish and the larder tally rises.

events.text: White seal pups lie on the high ledge among the grey adults. The croon carries across the water at dusk. You count eleven and write the number on the slate.
events.cause: The player counts pups from the tender with no engine; the tally on the slate rises.

events.text: The autumn gale takes the loose planks from the yard heap and puts some on the beach. A few are split, but most are fine. You gather them by the fire.
events.cause: Surge and wind push heaps; the player and robots re-stack the yard; stock numbers drop then rise as heaps are re-carried.

events.text: Winter is not a punishment. The island rests, and so can you. Keep the lamp lit.
events.cause: First frost on the yard; a crate on the tender; the paper panel opens.

events.text: The lamp oil is nearly gone. For a night the headland is dark. You light a candle in the hut window and wait for the next boat.
events.cause: The stump lamp goes dark at dusk; a candle burns in the hut window; the lamp lights again after the oil crate arrives.

events.text: A hard clear night. Stars crowd the sky to the water's edge. Frost on the planks. You stand on the strand and cannot stop looking up.
events.cause: The sky clock draws a deep star field and a moon-silvered sea; a frost sparkle on the jetty planks.

events.text: The year ends. The report is a plain card with four lines: profit, wildlife, happiness and resilience. None is the right one. You have a roof, a boat, a lamp, and a year behind you.
events.cause: A paper card is pinned to the hut door: four bars, each with one sentence.

events.text: Wedged on the high rock, a crate and a small motor wrapped in oilcloth. The oilcloth is dry. You lash both to the thwart and row home.
events.cause: The player rows to the outer skerry, loads the crate and motor, fits the motor on the stern at the jetty; the boat speed readout rises.
events.source: beat 1 pattern (Mysterious Island): an unordered crate

events.text: The plank you fitted today will hold. The one beside it wants a longer nail.
events.cause: A green bottle rolls on the wave edge; the player lifts it and unrolls the paper.
events.source: town list: gift_day.js BOTTLES[0], quoted unedited

events.text: Between the second and third autumn storm there is always one still day. Plan your roof for it.
events.cause: A bottle in the weed at the high-tide line.
events.source: town list: gift_day.js BOTTLES[1], quoted unedited

events.text: The seals come to the east rocks when the water is coldest. Leave them room and they will stay.
events.cause: A bottle against the jetty post.
events.source: town list: gift_day.js BOTTLES[2], quoted unedited

events.text: The first rows come up thin, and the wind takes the rest. You write down what went wrong and sow again in the spring, with a windbreak of net.
events.cause: The rows are thin, salt-burnt; the player puts nets on stakes; the robot carries rope and net.
events.source: beat 5 (Robinson Crusoe): the first harvest fails

events.text: At the lowest spring tide the ribs of an old hull stand on the highest head of the reef. Dark timber, bolted, never burned. A faded plate on one rib bears the small mark.
events.cause: At -0.7 m the reef head shows ribs; the tender stays 24 m off the reef ring; the plate shows the mark.

events.text: On the bare rock a single wind-bent tree. Tied round its trunk is a faded strip of cloth with the same knot as the tender's ropes.
events.cause: The player rows to the bare rock (about 100 s); the tree's trunk shows a knotted cloth strip.

events.text: You watch the tender tie up with no hand on it. The ropes lie in neat figure-eights on the jetty. When you coil one yourself it comes out the same.
events.cause: The unmanned tender lands, throws no crew, and lays its own ropes; the player coils one the same way.

events.text: Stakes, frame, walls, roof. By the end of the second day the cottage stands. It smells of wet wood and fresh paint. You sleep in it for the first time.
events.cause: Visible stages: stakes, frame, walls, roof; the player and robots carry planks; a lit window at dusk.

events.text: A rainbow after rain. It lands on the east rocks, and every bird on the ledge lifts at once, then settles. You stay until it fades.
events.cause: A rainbow on the lamp knoll side; birds lift and settle.

events.text: A tangled net comes in on the tide with half a dozen crab pots in it. You spend the afternoon freeing it. The crab you keep. The net you hang to dry.
events.cause: A net lies on the wrack line; the player and a robot cut it free and drag it to the yard.

events.text: A bank of driftwood lies along the strand after the spring tide. You and the carriers work three mornings. By the end of the week the yard heap is a wall of grey boards.
events.cause: A grey line of driftwood at the high-tide mark; robots carry loads of two; the yard heap grows visibly.

events.text: A green glass float rolls up the beach. It is whole, and cold, and there is not a scratch on it. You hold it to the lamp, and it makes a small green moon.
events.cause: A green float in the wrack; the player lifts it; the glass tally rises by one.

events.text: The sorter robot brings a basket of tin lids and pieces of metal. It sorts them in three clean heaps with small bright sounds, and rolls back for more.
events.cause: A sorter robot drops a basket and sorts it by metal type at the yard; the metal count rises as each heap is added.

events.text: You open one of the plain envelopes. It holds a single sheet: The north wall will not stand a gale unbraced. Brace it before autumn. The mark is in the corner.
events.cause: The player slits an envelope from the shelf; a paper panel; the north wall shows brace marks in chalk.
events.source: beat 14 pattern (New Atlantis): a gift of knowledge

events.text: Another envelope: A seal on the east rocks will not bite. A hide to the north will let you watch without a stir. It is only a note, and it is exactly right.
events.cause: The second envelope is opened at the hut table; a paper panel; the hide site on the north shelf is chalked.

events.text: At the hut table you read the office letter again. There is no street on it, only two numbers. You find the same two numbers on the sea chart. They are the island you are sitting on.
events.cause: The letter and the chart side by side on the hut table; the notebook pins the island at the two numbers.
events.source: owner idea: the New Life Inheritance twist

events.text: When the first carrier starts, you see a small mark stamped low on its side. It is the same mark that closes the office letter. It may be chance. It is only a mark.
events.cause: The player wipes grease from the chassis of a started robot; the mark shows; the notebook adds a stamp.

events.text: The tender brings the shed door you asked for. Its hinges are a size too small for the posts, and nothing in the crate says why. You drill new holes, hang it a little crooked, and it shuts.
events.cause: The tender lands a door crate; the hinge pins miss the post holes; the player re-drills and hangs the door by hand.

events.text: A coil of rope comes that is thicker than the jetty cleats. It is good rope. You open the cleat slots with a rasp over one afternoon, and then it holds the tender fast.
events.cause: A thick coil on the jetty; it will not seat in the cleats; the player rasps the slots wider and makes it fast.

events.text: In the lidded box at the landing lies a blanket, and under it a second one, folded the same way. Whoever packed the box allowed for the first to be wet through.
events.cause: The player lifts the lid of the box at the landing in rain: a damp blanket on top, a dry one beneath; no note.

events.text: The delivery crates have a rope handle at each end and two wooden runners underneath. One person can drag one up the sand without a barrow. They were built for someone working alone.
events.cause: The player drags a crate from the tender up the sand on its runners by one rope handle; the two-man lift is optional.

events.text: The collector's sorting rack has one low shelf set just above the high-water mark. Light dry kindling gathers there, because it is the first bin the tide cannot reach. It is the shelf you needed for the stove.
events.cause: A robot drops sorted loads into the rack; the lowest bins flood on the spring tide; the shelf above the line stays dry and fills with kindling.

events.text: You hand a parcel back, unopened. The tender takes it and goes. On its next visit the ordinary supplies arrive just as before, and nothing is said about the one that went back.
events.cause: The player carries an unopened parcel down to the tender; it lifts it aboard and leaves; the next call lands the usual crates.

events.text: The first proper rain runs the whole length of the mended gutter and drops into the barrel in one clear rope. Under the eave you hear the barrel's note drop lower as it fills.
events.cause: Rain on the hut roof; the water follows the full length of the repaired gutter into the barrel; the barrel's water mark rises.

events.text: At the bottom of a low tide the missing second oar lies under the landing, wedged between two stones and perfectly sound. The tender can be rowed straight again.
events.cause: The water drops below the landing; the player lifts the oar from between two stones and fits it in the tender's rowlock.

events.text: The tender delivers the long bench in two halves, each too short for the spot. You can join them with a plate, or give each cove its own seat. Either way the evening goes better sitting down.
events.cause: The tender lands two bench halves; the player either bolts a plate between them or carries one to each cove.

choices.label: Join the halves with a plate
Give each cove its own seat

events.text: The water butt has frozen at the tap. Breakfast starts with a bucket, a kettle and a short wait at the stove while the ice lets go. By noon the tap runs again.
events.cause: A hard frost; the butt tap is white with ice; the player carries a kettle of hot water to thaw it and fills the bucket from the barrel top.

events.text: On the last short afternoon the low sun reaches the windowsill where your first seedlings have come up. For ten minutes the tray is gold, and then the light moves on.
events.cause: A low sun at midwinter climbs the sill; the seed tray in the window lights; the seedlings show as small green rows.

events.text: The tender lands a stack of dry boards under a tarp, unasked. The wrack line is full of wet ones. You can take the dry boards, or hand them back and make do with what the sea left.
events.cause: The tender ties up and the boards sit strapped on the jetty; the wrack line shows swollen planks; the player lifts the first strap or turns to the beach.

choices.label: Take the dry boards
Hand them back and salvage the wet ones

events.text: The wet boards come up the beach by barrow, one at a time. It takes the whole afternoon and your hands are raw by the end. By dusk the yard stack stands tall, and the boards will be dry by the end of the week.
events.cause: A barrow trip after trip from the wrack line to the yard; boards are laid on stickers to dry; the stack grows by hand.

events.text: The tender comes on its usual day as if nothing had been handed back. The crates are the ones you ordered, the ropes are tied the same, and no note mentions the boards.
events.cause: The tender lands on its appointed tide with the ordered crates and ties its figure-eights; nothing is left or removed.

events.text: One card in the catalogue has been turned over, blank side up. Track links are no longer made. The shelf slot is empty. The carriers will want a spare before long.
events.cause: On the shelf of cards in the jetty store, the card for track links is turned over and its slot is bare.
events.source: beat 21 pattern (Machine Stops): a spare part that no longer exists

events.text: Some things are no longer made. That is not your fault. There is always another way to make a thing, and you have the hands for it.
events.cause: A crate on the tender with a paper panel; the shelf card is turned over.

variants.trust: You have used what was given well.
variants.distrust: You have not spent much. That is fine. It will wait.

events.text: A crate is waiting at the jetty. The tender is tied up beside it, empty. In the crate is the very thing you meant to order tomorrow.
events.cause: The player walks to the jetty at dawn: a crate and no boat seen; the ledger shows the order as already filled.

events.text: You have now seen the small mark on a crate, a carrier and a cairn stone. It is the same. A letter might say what it means. It will not, but it is a good thing to have noticed.
events.cause: The notebook page of stamps shows three marks side by side; the player can lay the drawer paper beside them.

events.text: You have noticed the mark. Many do, in the end. It means only that this came from a place that cares how it lands.
events.cause: A crate with the mark on the lid; the paper panel opens only on the investigate path.

events.text: You lay the papers from the drawer beside the crate lid. The signature on the estate papers and the mark on the crate are the same shape. A coincidence is a kind of answer.
events.cause: The player lays a paper next to a crate lid on the hut table; the camera lingers on the two marks.

events.text: You put the office's letter in the outgoing crate with a short note. The tender takes it. There is no way to say what you hope to hear.
events.cause: The player places an envelope in the outgoing crate at the jetty; the tender takes it away.

events.text: The office writes back, formal and dull. Our archive is incomplete: we hold no record of the matter either way. The letter you hold is on our paper, though not in our book. We are not permitted to say more.
events.cause: A returned envelope on the next tender; formal paper with a quay-town postmark and a different signature again.
events.source: owner idea: no such man in any record

events.text: On a clear night, a faint light blinks on the horizon: three short, one long. It is the same pattern as your horn. Someone else has been given an island.
events.cause: From the lamp knoll at night, a distant point of light flashes the horn's pattern; the chart shows a new parcel.

events.text: You are not the only one. Others have islands, and many have not looked up yet. You might help them, or you might not. Both have been done.
events.cause: A crate on the tender; a paper panel; the chart's new parcel is outlined.

variants.share: Some of them will need rope before the winter.

events.text: A small boat comes by on a calm morning. Someone asks, with gestures, for rope and a tin of seed. You carry the coil and the tin to the jetty and they row off with a wave.
events.cause: A boat at the jetty; the player and a hauler carry a coil of rope; the rope heap in the yard shrinks.
events.source: beat 24 (Looking Backward): a neighbour asks for rope and seed

events.text: A basket on the jetty, left in the night: a bag of dried apples and a coil of good line. The tie on the basket is a knot you do not know.
events.cause: A basket sits on the jetty at dawn, with a knot of unfamiliar pattern; the stock and larder rise when carried up.

events.text: The far light does not blink for a week. You look every night. On the eighth it comes back, a little dimmer, and your own lamp is lit again in answer.
events.cause: From the lamp knoll, the far point does not blink for seven nights; on the eighth it returns.

events.text: A winter gale lifts the corner of the hut roof. In the morning you and a carrier carry planks and lay them back in the dry. The rain keeps off the stove for the night.
events.cause: A roof strip lifts; the player and a robot carry planks and nail them back; the planks counter drops as they are fixed.

events.text: A carrier has stalled on the bar at the turn of the tide. Its light is amber. You wade out with a rope while the water gathers round your boots.
events.cause: A robot sits stopped at the lowest cells of the bar as the tide turns; its light is amber.

events.text: Together you and a second carrier haul the stalled one over the sill with a rope and a plank. It starts again at once, wet but sound. The bar is empty and the tide comes in.
events.cause: The player and a robot pull on a rope; the stalled robot's light goes green; they cross before the water.

events.text: You spend a wet afternoon brushing moss off a carrier and repainting the worn patches. It is blue now where it was grey. The mark on its side is clean.
events.cause: The player scrubs a robot with a brush; its panels change colour; a mossy strip is cleared.

events.text: A carrier's track link has worn through. There is no spare in the catalogue now. You take one from the Hoard, a plain link with a small mark, and fit it with your own hands.
events.cause: The player carries a track link from the depot; fits it; the robot's tracks run again.

events.text: At the back of the depot, a locker with a brass lock. Your key turns. The lock is not meant for your key and takes it anyway. Inside: a lamp wick, a coil of line, and a chart cut to the shape of the table.
events.cause: The player opens the locker with the brass key; the objects are laid out on the depot table.

events.text: After the storm, a battered boat, two cold travellers, and a hungry dog. You give soup and dry blankets. They leave a bag of oats and say little.
events.cause: A boat grounds after the storm; two figures by your fire; one more tally on the guest slate; a bag of oats in the larder.
events.source: beat 13 (New Atlantis): kind welcome to strangers

events.text: You run the motor too close. The seals slide into the water in a rush. The ledge is empty by the time the wake settles, and you are sorry.
events.cause: The motor wake reaches the ledge; seals slip into the sea; the tally on the slate drops.

events.text: From the hide you count thirty-one seals and seven pups. The notebook records it. The slate by the hide door shows a longer line than last year.
events.cause: The player sits in the hide; a tally of seals and pups rises on the slate.

events.text: The long evenings are back. The strand is warm, and the water is almost swimmable. A boat brings a family for the afternoon. They are counted and leave smiling.
events.cause: A boat lands at the jetty; guests walk the strand; the slate and cash line rise.

events.text: A week of fog. The horn sounds from the dark, the tender comes and goes by sound. You sit by the fire and mend nets and do not mind.
events.cause: Fog covers the table; the delivery marker slides two days; the horn sounds more often.

events.text: A still week of frost. Nothing arrives. The lamp is lit, and the stove ticks. You read the same page twice and it is enough.
events.cause: Frost on the yard; smoke rises straight from the chimney; the robots rest at the post.

events.text: The first swallows cross the sound. The turf is green again. You walk the strand and find three new seedlings in the sand where there were none.
events.cause: Seedlings on the dune, a flight of swallows over the yard.

events.text: The motor coughs and stops halfway home. The tide takes you gently into the bay and you row the last stretch. It is a slow evening, and the sea is kind.
events.cause: The engine stops; the player rows; a tide drift carries the boat toward the lee shore.

events.text: In the long evenings you and the carriers build a narrow skiff with a pole-drive engine from a Hoard motor and a keel of old oak. It is loud, and it is quick.
events.cause: Visible stages: keel, ribs, planking, engine on a pivot; the player and robots carry planks; launch down the slip.
events.source: beat 9 (Swiss Family Robinson): finds turned into tools

events.text: The first rain fills a barrel faster than you expect. Do not mind the small leak. Mend it on a dry morning.
events.cause: A bottle at the tide wrack after rain.
events.source: town list: gift_day.js BOTTLES[3], quoted unedited

events.text: A lamp that burns all night will not be missed. A lamp that burns one hour at dusk will be seen.
events.cause: A bottle on the strand at dawn.
events.source: town list: gift_day.js BOTTLES[4], quoted unedited

events.text: The third winter will be a long one. Salt what you can in the autumn.
events.cause: A bottle in the weed after an autumn gale.

events.text: In the hardest week of winter you take the coat from its hook and put it on. It fits as if made for you. In the left pocket, the same worn pencil.
events.cause: The player lifts the coat from the hook; the player's silhouette gains a coat colour.

events.text: Another year, another card. Fewer boats, more of your own. The bars are different shapes this year, and it is up to you which you like best.
events.cause: A new paper card on the hut door: four bars and a longer line on resilience.

events.text: At dawn the three carriers fan out along the strand in a line, their lights green. It looks like a small slow parade. You take your tea to the jetty and watch.
events.cause: Robots leave the yard at first light; the status lights show green; track marks appear on the sand.

events.text: At the lowest tide the rock pools are open like small gardens. You find crabs, a starfish and a limpet the size of a coin. You put them back and keep a handful of mussels.
events.cause: Pools on the low shelf; the player kneels; the larder tally rises by a little.

events.text: A heap of kelp on the strand after the spring tide. You fork it onto the beds and the garden drinks it in. The smell is strong, and by the weekend it is gone.
events.cause: Brown kelp on the wrack line; the player and a robot fork it into barrows and carry it to the beds.

events.text: Out in the sound a gannet folds and drops like a white arrow into the sea. Another, then six. You stop the oars and watch the water close over them.
events.cause: White birds fold and plunge off the lee shore; the oars are shipped.

events.text: Dolphins come alongside the boat and ride the bow wave for a full minute, curving over and under it. They leave as suddenly as they came. You are grinning.
events.cause: Grey fins arc around the bow; the wake lifts; the camera follows them off.

events.text: At first light an otter hunts along the east cove, brown and low, diving with a roll. It brings a crab to a rock and eats it there, quite unhurried, and goes.
events.cause: A brown shape at the cove at dawn; ripples; a crab on a rock.

events.text: A long soft rain on the canvas. The barrel fills by the hour. You sit in the doorway with tea and watch the level rise, and do not mind the wet.
events.cause: Rain on the roof; a trickle into the barrel; the litre count rises with the water line.

events.text: A blustery night. In the morning a drift of boards, a barrel and a coil of line lie along the wrack. A small haul, and a good start to the day.
events.cause: A light haul on the wrack line; robots go out at first light; heaps grow in the yard.

events.text: A hard frost. The barrel has a lid of ice and the tap will not run. You melt snow in the kettle, and the carriers stay under cover until the sun comes.
events.cause: Ice on the barrel; kettle steam; robots wait at the post.

events.text: In the long dusk you mend a net by the stove. The twine is stiff, the knot is slow, but by lamp-lighting the tear is shut. It is a small pleasure.
events.cause: A net on stakes by the stove; the tear closes; the rope count does not change.

events.text: The horn sounds at dawn, an hour before the tender should be in. You hurry down to the jetty and the boat is already tying up, the crate waiting on the thwart.
events.cause: The horn; the tender lands early; the crate is carried up the beach by the player and a robot.

events.text: A carrier has gone down the wrong side of a rock, and stopped with its light amber. You turn it round by hand and set it on its route, and it goes on as if nothing had happened.
events.cause: A robot wedged at a rock; the player turns it; the light goes green.

events.text: The rack at the jetty is not full this week. Two slots stand empty and the tender has no crate for you. You make do with what the yard heap has.
events.cause: The delivery rack at the jetty has dark slots; the tender passes without landing.

events.text: A hundred gulls on the roof of the yard shed, all facing into the wind. You walk round them. They do not mind you at all, only the wind.
events.cause: Gulls lined along the shed roof; the player walks the yard.

events.text: The office letter and its reply carry the same quay-town postmark, down to the same smudge, though months lie between them and a gale between those. You turn them over and put them away.
events.cause: Two envelopes laid side by side on the jetty store table; the smudge lines up.
events.source: owner idea: postmarks from one place

events.text: On the office letter and on its reply, a different name is signed at the foot each time, in a different hand. Not one is used twice. You line them up and give up trying to make a person of it.
events.cause: The two sheets on the hut table, signatures circled in pencil; the notebook has a page of crossed-out guesses.
events.source: owner idea: staff names that never repeat

events.text: Inside the lamp stump, a black telephone you had not seen. Its number is the one at the foot of the office letter. It rings at dusk, eleven times, and stops. When you lift it there is a faint hum, and the sea.
events.cause: The stump door is open; a phone on the wall rings; the player lifts the receiver; the lamp light flickers once.
events.source: owner idea: a number that rings at the lamp

events.text: Behind the shelf of envelopes is a narrow door, and the brass key opens it. A small back room holds a grey filing cabinet with nine folders. Each has a pair of numbers and a page of weather. None has a name.
events.cause: The player turns the key in a narrow door behind the shelf; a cabinet and nine folders are laid on the table.
events.source: owner idea: files for other islands

events.text: You lay the personal letter beside the letters from the crates. The turns of phrase, the way each ends with no name, the small mark in the corner: it is the same hand, line for line. You do not know what to make of it.
events.cause: The personal letter and three crate letters side by side on the hut table; the marks line up.
events.source: owner idea: P2 phrasing and mark match L1 to L12

events.text: On a still evening you notice the hut door has no handle on the outside. It opens only from within, or by the long bar of the brass key. Beside it is a small hatch with a worn sill, the right size for a crate.
events.cause: Camera rests on the hut door from outside: a plain plate where a handle would be, the key turning in a bar, and a low delivery hatch beside it with a scuffed sill.
events.source: owner idea: never good at walking through a front door

events.text: A box of long nails arrives for a roof you mended with pegs and boards last spring. They are good nails. You put them on the shelf for the next roof.
events.cause: A nail box on the hut table; the roof it was meant for is already mended; it goes on the shelf beside the rest.

events.text: A crate is left on the jetty just before the rain, and no one is there to carry it up. The label runs and the paper swells. What is inside is only a little damp.
events.cause: The tender lands a crate and leaves; rain on the jetty boards runs the ink on the label; the player carries it in.

events.text: The brass key fits the lock of the old boat shed at the jetty, and turns without a catch. Inside the keyhole the brass is worn smooth, by far more turns than you have given it.
events.cause: The player tries the brass key in the boat shed lock; it opens; a close look shows the keyhole polished by long use.

events.text: At low water the oldest pile of the jetty shows the small plain mark below the weed. The newest timber has a saw and a leaf branded on it, from the mill in the woods. The planks between have no mark at all.
events.cause: At a low tide the player reads the jetty piles from the boat: one stamped, one branded with the woods mill, the rest bare.

events.text: In the sorting shed every storage bay has a stamped number in a neat row. One bay is divided by pencil lines that wander, with a few tally strokes in the corner. It was made by hand and left as it was.
events.cause: The player walks the depot shed; the bays are numbered by a press; one is divided in pencil with crooked lines and tallies.

events.text: The old slipway cradle takes the tender as if it were shaped for it. But the painted waterline marks on the cradle sit a hand lower than the tender floats. Whatever it was built for sat deeper in the water.
events.cause: The player hauls the tender onto the slipway cradle; it seats exactly; the old paint marks on the cradle show below the tender's own waterline.

events.text: A spare lens for the lamp comes wrapped in a length of carpet. It is the close diamond weave from the cafe doorway in the loom town, but a thread of teal runs through this one.
events.cause: A crate of lamp parts at the jetty; the packing carpet unrolled on the yard grass: grey diamonds with one teal thread.

events.text: At the far cove two sets of iron mooring rings are sunk in the rock, one rusted and one bright. The delivery chart shows a single stop here.
events.cause: The player lands at the far cove and finds a rusted row and a bright row of rings; the delivery chart on the table shows one mark.

events.text: One plank of the jetty deck is newer than the rest and bare: no mark, no number. The saw cuts are rough and the nails are the wrong sort. Somebody else mended this, and not with you in mind.
events.cause: The player runs a hand along the jetty deck and stops at a plank with ragged saw cuts and mismatched nails; no stamp anywhere.

events.text: The bigger boat is launched. Its hold takes a stack of repair timber on one side and crossing provisions on the other, and it sits level. For the first time one trip does both jobs.
events.cause: The new hull slides off the slip; planks go in the port bay, sacks and water kegs in the starboard; the waterline marks stay clear.

events.text: You open the landing for one weekend and no longer. A boat each morning, fourteen visitors in all, counted at the rail and never named. You choose what they may do: the shore path, the hide, or supper on the beach.
events.cause: Two boats land; a tally ticks at the rail; visitors walk only where the player has opened a path; the landing closes on Sunday evening.

choices.label: Open the shore path
Open the hide for the seals
Set supper out on the beach

events.text: A bird has nested in the best timber rack, just as the boards are dry enough to use. You work round it with the second-best planks and leave the rack alone until the chicks fly.
events.cause: A nest in the upper timber rack with a bird sitting; the player stacks the next boards on the lower rack; the nest stays.

events.text: The first boat from the next island brings cuttings wrapped in wet wool, with a twist of paper that says only which end goes in the ground. By supper they are in a row.
events.cause: A boat from the neighbouring island lands; cuttings in damp wool; the player plants them along the yard wall.

events.text: You cleared the east ledge of drift last spring. Now a seal has hauled out on the warm rock beside the cleared path, and takes no notice of who passes. You walk it slowly, and are not seen.
events.cause: A seal on the cleared ledge in sun; the path beside it is bare of tangled driftwood and nets; the seal count rises by one.

events.text: A visiting boat stays for supper. Both sides of your table are used and one end of the bench is a crate. The boat leaves on the evening tide, and the plates come back counted.
events.cause: A small boat ties up at the jetty; guests eat at the yard table; they leave at the turn of the tide; the guest tally rises.

events.text: The tide cuts off the flat picnic rock early. Collecting the crockery becomes a rowing trip, plates stacked in the stern and the tender sitting low. Nothing breaks.
events.cause: The rising tide covers the causeway to the flat rock; the player rows out and ferries the plates back in two loads.
events.source: critic review v2: 20 seasonal events; needs: a flat picnic rock below the landing (placeholder: any rock)

events.text: At dusk the old speaker on the pole plays its usual tune while people stand at the landing. Nobody asked for it. The tune ends, the boats go on loading, and the evening settles.
events.cause: The speaker on its post by the jetty plays at dusk; guests at the landing pause and carry on; no lamp or switch is shown.
events.source: critic review v2: 20 seasonal events; needs: speaker prop (conditional on flag speaker_prop)

events.text: A storm leaves a whole timber gate on the beach, swinging on one hinge as the surf pulls at it. It is good oak. Someone's boundary has gone elsewhere, and you have a gate.
events.cause: After the storm a gate lies at the tideline held by one hinge; the player drags it above the weed and takes off the hinge.

events.text: Kelp winds round a collector track and drags it in circles. By morning the collector has worn a neat semicircle in the sand, and a bare patch of shore beside it.
events.cause: Kelp wound on one track; the collector turns on the spot until it is cut free; a smooth arc is left in the wet sand.

events.text: A neighbour offers apples for dry storage just as your own harvest comes in. Your loft takes both, but only just, and you spend a day on slats and string so that none of them touch.
events.cause: A neighbour's boat lands with crates of apples; the loft shelves fill; the player lays slats and strings between the rows.

events.text: A spring tide lifts the repaired hull clear of its cradle and sets it down an inch to port. The chocks were cut for exactly this, and it comes down true.
events.cause: At a spring high the repaired hull floats free of the cradle chocks, drifts a little and settles back on the chocks.
events.source: critic review v2: 20 seasonal events; needs: a repaired hull on a cradle (the skiff on the slip)

events.text: Frost shows a pale strip across the yard where the ground stays dark. It runs past the place you thought the buried pipe ended. You move your stake twenty paces and dig there.
events.cause: A hard frost at dawn; a dark warm strip crosses the white yard beyond the old stake; the player reburies the pipe plan.

events.text: On a clear night you can see the far landing light from the chair at the hut window, without getting up. It blinks three short and one long. You lean back and let it count for you.
events.cause: The clear winter night; the far light blinks its pattern in the window frame; the chair faces it.

events.text: Fog holds the tender offshore. You hear its horn, three short and one long, while you finish the shelf you were mending. The crate will come in on the next tide, or the one after.
events.cause: Fog on the water; the horn pattern sounds from the grey; the player keeps working and the tender does not appear.

events.text: The boats come less often now. This was always going to happen. You have more than you think.
events.cause: A crate with the first spaced delivery; the chalk board at the jetty shows wider gaps.

events.text: You count the boats on the chalk board: one in four days, not one in two. The horn is heard less. When one comes you go down to the jetty to meet it.
events.cause: The chalk lines on the jetty board are drawn wider apart; the delivery rack has fewer slots lit.

events.text: The glass card is turned over, blank side up. No more panes by boat. You hold a green float to the light and think of a wall made of bottles.
events.cause: On the shelf the glass card turns over; the delivery rack loses a slot.

events.text: You and the carriers lay a wall of bottles in mortar, the sun coming through green and blue. It is warm inside, and the stove light dances.
events.cause: Visible stages: footing, bottle courses laid in mortar, the sun through green glass; the glass count falls as bottles go in.
events.source: beat 9 (Swiss Family Robinson): every find becomes a tool

events.text: The engine card goes. The last motor part that came by boat is the one you have. You oil it and wrap it in cloth.
events.cause: The engine card on the shelf turns over; the player wraps the motor in oilcloth.

events.text: No boat for a week. The rack is empty and the horn is silent. You live on what the yard heap and the hoard have. It is enough, and it is quiet.
events.cause: Seven mornings with no tender; the chalk board gets a long gap; the yard heaps carry the work.

events.text: The lamp goes dark for a week. A wick has gone, and none comes by boat. You and a carrier climb the knoll with a wick from the Hoard, and light it again at dusk.
events.cause: The stump lamp is dark at dusk for seven nights; the player and a robot carry the wick up the path and relight.
events.source: beat 21 extra: a lighthouse that goes dark

events.text: The harbour log at the jetty store has stopped being filled in. The last entry is in the same plain hand as always. The pages after it are blank.
events.cause: The player opens the log at the jetty store; the last filled page is a few days old; the rest are empty.
events.source: beat 21 extra: a harbour log that stops being filled

events.text: The glass falls and falls. The gulls leave the sky. The carriers hurry to their post. A slow round eddy begins to turn off the west shore, and you watch it from the knoll.
events.cause: Barometer pill falls; gulls leave; a foamy eddy turns off the lee shore; the camera eases over.

events.text: In the night the sea lets go. In the morning the whole strand is heaped with timber, crates, barrels, and a great old hull lying on the sheltered stretch. There is more than you can carry in a year.
events.cause: A tidal swirl and a surge leave 900 or so pieces on the home strand; a big hulk lies near the camp; robots and the player start carrying.

events.text: Everything the sea has been holding came at once. It is a lot. You do not have to keep it all, and you do not have to decide today. Sort it slowly. Share what you cannot use.
events.cause: A crate on the morning boat; the paper panel opens on the heaped shore.

events.text: You and the carriers take a few boards off the hulk each morning. The old boat gives its ribs slowly. In the evenings you sort the day's bolts into jars.
events.cause: Visible work on the hulk: boards unbolted, carried across the beach by player and robot, jars of bolts on a shelf.

events.text: You load a boat with timber, rope and barrels, and send it to the far light. The neighbour comes the next morning with a bag of seed and a hand to shake. Both islands are bigger.
events.cause: The boat is loaded by the player and robots at the jetty; stock drops as crates are lifted aboard; the neighbour returns with seed.
events.source: beat 11 (Swiss Family Robinson): neighbours share the work by skill

events.text: You were slow with the heaps. The tide takes the loose ones back, and some of the timber floats away. You are sorry for the waste. The hulk is still there, and the best planks.
events.cause: After about two days the loose heaps thin and drift away on the ebb; stock drops only by what was not carried.

events.text: In the wash, a glass float with the mark etched inside, where no tool could reach. You turn it in the light. It is whole.
events.cause: A green float in a heap; the mark shows inside as you hold it up.

events.text: In the hulk, a hand-cranked radio. When you wind it, there is only a slow tone: three short, one long. No words. You switch it off and the silence is large.
events.cause: The player cranks a radio from the hulk; a tone pattern like the horn plays; no voice.
events.source: beat 22 pattern (Machine Stops): a small voice, here only a tone

events.text: With the hulk's ribs and the Hoard's tools you set up a workshop by the slip. Benches, a lathe, a rack of old keels. There is room for two, and a carrier sits at the end of the bench.
events.cause: Visible stages: floor, benches, a roof; the player and robots carry the lathe from the hulk.
events.source: owner idea: sort and repair into a workshop

events.text: The beds come up thick this year. The windbreak holds, and the rain was kind. You eat well. The rest goes in jars on the shelf.
events.cause: Rows of green; jars on the shelf; the larder tally rises.

events.text: A small boat lands from the far island. Three visitors, counted, a gift of salt fish, a plan to meet in the spring. You show them the lamp.
events.cause: A boat lands at the jetty; three figures walk the path to the lamp; the guest slate gets three marks.

events.text: A crate from the neighbour has the small mark on the lid. They did not put it there. They hold the crate out to you and shrug, and so do you.
events.cause: The neighbour hands over a crate with the mark; the notebook adds a stamp.

events.text: A calm night after a storm, and a boat at your jetty: the neighbour's roof has lifted and they need planks. You load them with a carrier at one end and the neighbour at the other.
events.cause: The player and a hauler robot carry planks to a waiting boat; the planks counter drops as they go.

events.text: On the chart, a small island with a sandy cove, a low hill and a freshwater lens. It is for sale at a price you can nearly meet. You write the number on the slate.
events.cause: A survey voyage returns; the chart shows a new parcel with a price tag.

events.text: You count the cash on the table. Enough for a small one. You buy the island by cash, since credit cannot buy land. A new key, a new gate, a new beach. Two homes.
events.cause: The cash line falls by the purchase; the chart fills in the new parcel; a second jetty appears on the map.
events.source: owner idea: stay, move or buy

events.text: In the wash a small party lands from a drifted boat, tired and shy. You give a meal and a bed. In the morning they ask the way to the nearest island and you tell them.
events.cause: A beached boat, a fire, three tallies; a boat leaves by dawn.

events.text: The ledge is full this autumn. Sixty seals, a score of pups. You count from the hide for two evenings to be sure, and the number is the same both times.
events.cause: The tally on the hide slate rises by fifteen; the lamp beam shows the full ledge.

events.text: A lesser storm brings a modest haul: a pile of planks and two barrels. You and the carriers sort it by noon, and have the heaps stacked by dusk.
events.cause: Heaps on the wrack line; the player carries one end of planks with a robot at the other.

events.text: A thin green curtain moves across the north on a clear winter night. The robots stop and you stand with them in the cold. It lasts twenty minutes and is gone.
events.cause: The sky clock draws a faint green curtain over the north horizon.

events.text: When the shelf is empty, look under the rock where the seals sleep.
events.cause: A bottle in the lee of the east cove.

events.text: Someone is hoping this place is kind to you. That is all this note is for.
events.cause: A bottle on the beach at dawn.
events.source: town list: gift_day.js BOTTLES[5], quoted unedited

events.text: A last envelope on the shelf: The road you built to the hide will flood in the third spring. Move it uphill. The mark is in the corner, and this time the paper is warm.
events.cause: The player opens the envelope at the hut table; the hide track is chalked on the hillside.

events.text: A visitor from the loom town stops at the hut door. So you have family with an island, she says, and laughs kindly. Nobody on our hill knew of one. And that office on the quay: the brass plate has been blank for years.
events.cause: A visitor stands at the hut door and makes her own guess; she looks past you at the coat on the hook.
events.source: owner idea: no such man exists in any record

events.text: Moss grows on the tops of the carriers. You scrub them each spring, and one of them lies still for a week under a sprig of ivy while you decide whether to wake it.
events.cause: Moss on robot panels; one robot idle at the post; its light amber.

events.text: Two carriers carry a long beam across the bar at the same time, step for step, one end each. You walk behind and call out the tide. They do not need the call, but it is good to say.
events.cause: Two robots carry a beam across the bar; the heap in the yard rises when they arrive.

events.text: Caught between the isles in a rising wind, the boat rides high and wet. You head into the sea and it takes the spray. At the jetty you tie up and laugh from the cold.
events.cause: A heavy sea, a wet boat, a rocking camera; the tender is tied up at the jetty.

events.text: A summer fair on the strand. Your neighbour sets a stall, there are lanterns of bottle glass, and a hundred small boats stand in the roads. You count the guests and pour the tea.
events.cause: Lanterns on the strand, a row of boats; the guest slate gets a long line of marks.

events.text: A big mat of kelp comes in on the surge. You and a carrier fork it onto the beds before the gulls get at it. The rows green up by the next week.
events.cause: Kelp on the strand; the player and a robot fork it into barrows; the beds darken.

events.text: Dolphins in the sound in the long evening. They come close to the jetty and stay for the length of a song. A guest on the boat holds her breath, and nobody says a word.
events.cause: Grey fins and soft clicks at the jetty; the guest slate gets a mark.

events.text: A night of gale, and you are warm in the hut with the stove, a book and the kettle ticking. The roof holds. The carriers sleep at the post. Outside, the sea shouts to itself.
events.cause: Storm on the glass; the stove glow; the robots at the post under cover.

events.text: On a sunny morning the three carriers stand in the yard with their panels turned to the light. You walk between them with your tea. The light on each one is steady green.
events.cause: Robots at the post; green lights; the charge bar fills.

events.text: A hard week. The wind comes round to the north and the stock bars drop one by one. You burn the worst of the wrack and wear the coat that fits.
events.cause: Smoke from the chimney; the yard heaps are smaller; a coat on the player.

events.text: A card falls from the shelf and nobody picks it up. The shelf has more empty slots than full. It looks like a shop at the end of a long day.
events.cause: A card on the floor; the shelf shows gaps; the delivery rack has fewer lit slots.

events.text: You take the boat out before sunrise. The sea is glass, the lamp a pale dot, and the whole table lies before you. Seals watch from far off, and you let the engine be quiet.
events.cause: A calm dawn on the water; mist at the sea edge; the wake is long and thin.

events.text: A sealed tin on the tideline. You prise it open. Inside: a hundred dry seeds and a handful of salt. You plant the seeds at the edge of the garden and write the date on a stake.
events.cause: A tin on the wrack; the player opens it; a stake is driven at the bed edge.

events.text: A thick fog, and the horn sounds from the jetty every few minutes. You stand on the knoll with a lantern, and a boat answers from far off, and then another.
events.cause: Fog bank over the table; horn blasts; a lantern on the knoll; boats answering.

events.text: Puffins stand outside their burrows on the far rock, each with a row of silver fish. They shuffle, bow and whirr off. You count twenty before the light goes.
events.cause: Black-and-white birds with bright bills on the turf; the bird tally rises.

events.text: One folder bears the numbers of the far light, and a page of weather for its coast. Another is thin, and says only: not yet. You shut the drawer gently.
events.cause: The player opens the drawer; one folder's numbers match the chart's new parcel; the notebook links them.

events.text: Your own folder is the thickest. It is dated three winters before the office letter reached you. The office wrote that it had no file of that name. You cannot tell which of them is wrong.
events.cause: The player lays the dated folder beside the reply on the hut table; the dates are circled.

events.text: To the owner of the island. This office was always unable to answer questions about the estate, and is not permitted to say why. It would, if it could. It is glad you are well. Please carry on as you are.
events.cause: A formal envelope on the tender with a quay-town postmark and one more name signed at the foot.
events.source: owner idea: it cannot tell you

events.text: The lamp stump has no door, only a hatch in its floor and a short ladder. The Hoard depot has a hatch too. Every way in is a hatch, as if the place was built for things to be sent in rather than people to turn up.
events.cause: The player climbs through the floor hatch of the lamp stump; the camera shows the other hatches on the map.

events.text: The new sea chart shows the old shoreline. After the wash the cove is a boat length shorter and the chart does not know. You pencil the new edge in yourself and leave the old one visible.
events.cause: A chart on the table; the cove outline is overdrawn; the player pencils the new line over the printed one.

events.text: Under the west skerry a tidal cave opens at low water. In it, an old crate gone black with salt. Inside its lid, where only someone opening it would look, is the small plain mark.
events.cause: At a spring low the player wades into a cave under the skerry; a salted crate; the stamp is on the inside of the lid, not the outside.

events.text: A notch cut in the headland rock lines up with nothing but open water. At the lowest tide the line ends on the black stumps of an old landing that nobody has mentioned.
events.cause: At a spring low the player sights through the notch on the lamp knoll; the water drops and square stumps appear on the line.

events.text: Each spare-parts drawer in the workshop has a scooped dip in the front for a thumb. The collector's claw cannot work them. The drawers were made for hands, and the hands are not yours.
events.cause: The player opens the workshop drawers; each has a thumb scoop; a collector's claw slides off the dip and cannot pull.

events.text: Under the hut floor, a box with the small plain mark. In it are beach stones, wrapped one by one in paper and packed to exactly the weight of a full parcel. Nothing says what they were for.
events.cause: The player lifts a loose board; a box with the stamp; stones in paper that balance a full parcel on the scale.

events.text: You saw a sound section free of the hulk and roll it onto chocks across the spring-tide line, bow to the sea. Then you leave it to the water, which is the only help it needs.
events.cause: The player cuts a hull section with the long saw, rolls it on logs onto chocks below the spring line, and ties it to a post.
events.source: critic review v2: act 3 goal (links to the hulk)

events.text: Over three spring tides the hull section lifts a little more each time, until it floats free on its line. Roofed and benched, it will be a workshop that rises and falls with the water.
events.cause: Each spring tide lifts the chocked hull a hand higher; on the third it swings free on its line; the player roofs and benches it.

events.text: Your first cast part is useful and far too bulky. It will not go through the workshop door. You can file it down, widen the door, or fit it where the door does not matter.
events.cause: A cast bracket sticks in the workshop doorway; the player files it, takes down the lintel to widen the door, or bolts it outside.

choices.label: File the part down
Widen the workshop door
Fit it outside, where it fits

events.text: On a quiet sailing day you carry a neighbour's crates across in your own boat. A handcart waits at their water's edge, already turned the right way for loading.
events.cause: The player's boat lands at a neighbour's shore; a handcart stands at the tideline; crates are loaded and the boat goes home.

events.text: A night gust peels back one corner of the workshop roof. The stored sailcloth is already folded by the door, and it covers the gap until morning. The boards underneath stay dry.
events.cause: A gust lifts a roof corner in the dark; the player drags the stored sailcloth over the gap and weights it with stones.

events.text: After a rough crossing a visiting crew borrows the shed overnight. In the morning it is swept, and a coiled towline hangs from the nail by the door, left for the next boat that needs one.
events.cause: A boat shelters at the jetty; the crew sleep in the shed; at dawn they cast off and a coiled towline is on the nail.

events.text: This is the last large parcel. After this, only small things come. The island can stand without them, and so can you. If you ever need anything, look at the shore.
events.cause: The last big crate is carried up the beach by the player and robots; the shelf shows fewer cards.

events.text: Six cards are left on the shelf: rope, tarp, seed, oil, a saw, a blanket. They are plain. They are all you need to start from.
events.cause: Six cards remain on the shelf; the rack has one slot lit; the tender comes once a week.

events.text: The shore is richer this year, as if it had been saving. A week of finds: rope, glass, a drum of oil, a crate with a pair of boots. You stack them neatly, and say nothing.
events.cause: The strand shows a string of finds after each spring tide; robots carry them in; the heaps in the yard grow.

events.text: You press the seed from the garden and the oil burns clean in the stump lamp. It smells of toast. It is the first night the lamp has been lit by your own hand alone.
events.cause: A small oil press in the yard; the player carries a can up to the lamp; the lamp lights at dusk.

events.text: A winter with no boats. The yard heaps carry you. The stove warms, the lamp is lit, and the evenings are long. It is enough, and it is quiet.
events.cause: Frost on the yard; the tender does not come; the stock bars hold.
events.source: beat 23 (Machine Stops): old skills win the winter

events.text: The neighbour comes with rope and seed after the winter, without being asked. You had given them the same in the spring of the year before. The boat leaves with fish.
events.cause: A boat lands at the jetty; two crates are carried up by the player and a hauler; the rope count rises.

events.text: Now you are the one with a full yard. A neighbour comes for planks and nails. You load them with a carrier at one end and the visitor at the other, and wave them off.
events.cause: The player and a hauler carry planks to the jetty; the planks counter drops; the boat sails.

events.text: A traveller walks up the beach after a storm, stays a week in the hut, and leaves a coil of line and a way of tying it. You never ask the name, and they do not say.
events.cause: A figure walks up the strand; hut smoke; later a coil on the jetty and an empty bunk.

events.text: One old carrier stops at its post and does not start. Its light is dark. You do not know how long it has worked. You lay a sheet of canvas over it and keep its parts for the others.
events.cause: A robot with a dark light sits at the post under a tarp; a few parts are carried to the workshop.

events.text: Winter, spring, summer: a carrier works the same strand every tide. You stop watching it, and it goes on. When you look up, the heap has grown.
events.cause: The robot makes its rounds; the yard heap rises one board at a time.

events.text: The last big storm of the year brings a handful of crates and long planks. You and the carriers go out at dawn. The tide is on the ebb.
events.cause: Heaps on the wrack line; the player and a robot carry a long beam between them.

events.text: On the longest day, your island hosts a small festival. Lanterns, boats, the neighbour's songs. You count two hundred guests and give them tea, and nobody goes hungry.
events.cause: Lanterns on the strand; boats lie in the roads; the guest slate fills.

events.text: The slate by the hide door shows the longest line yet: one hundred and four seals this autumn, thirty pups. You write the year beneath it.
events.cause: The tally on the slate rises; the lamp beam shows a full ledge.

events.text: The tender comes in at dawn, ties up, and leaves nothing. It waits a minute at the jetty, as if for something, and goes out again with the tide.
events.cause: An empty tender at the jetty at dawn, a short wait, and it leaves.

events.text: You made something. It does not matter what. It is yours, and it is good that it exists. The sea is still giving, if you are still looking.
events.cause: The year-four report is opened; the paper panel unrolls on the hut table.

events.text: A card from the office in the loom town: Your file is closed. The office is shutting its door in the spring. We wish the island well. The ink is blue, and the paper smells of rain.
events.cause: A card on the weekly tender; the loom town watermark and no mark.

events.text: The coat still hangs on its hook. You have worn it and hung it back a dozen times. It has taken the shape of your shoulders. The pencil is still in the pocket.
events.cause: A coat on a hook, in lamp light; the camera rests on it for a breath.

events.text: You sit in the chair that faces the lamp and watch the evening come. A tick in the table book, next to a low water. You add one of your own.
events.cause: The chair at the window; the tide book open on the table; the player's pencil makes a tick.

events.text: If you are reading this, the boats have thinned and you are still here. That was always the plan, and also the hope.
events.cause: A bottle on the tideline at dawn.

events.text: The lamp can be seen from further than you think. Keep it lit when it counts.
events.cause: A bottle against the jetty post at low light.

events.text: A bright, still fog in the morning. The sea and the sky are one colour. You stand on the strand and the carriers are shapes with green lights.
events.cause: A white fog bank over the table; green lights on robot shapes; the horn of the lamp sounds once.

events.text: A week of ice. The barrel freezes, the nets stiffen, and the tracks of the carriers print the yard white. You break the ice with a mallet and drink from the cistern.
events.cause: Ice on the barrel; frost on the yard; footprints and tracks across the white.

events.text: After rain, a double rainbow stands over the seal rock. The seals lift their heads. A gannet folds and drops through it into the sea.
events.cause: A double rainbow; seals raise heads; a gannet plunge.

events.text: Four years. The report card has four bars, and none is full, and none is empty. You look at the island and it looks back like a place that is yours.
events.cause: A fourth card on the hut door beside the other three; the island at dusk, lights in windows.

events.text: The same pools, and four years older. You know the limpets by sight. You take a few mussels, put the rest back, and carry them home in your hat.
events.cause: Rock pools at the lowest tide; a hat of mussels; the larder rises a little.

events.text: The dolphins are back, as they are each summer. They ride the bow wave and curve under it. You wave. It is not a thing you would have done in your first year.
events.cause: Fins at the bow; the camera follows the pod; the player waves.

events.text: You mend a net by the stove in the dusk, and teach a visitor the knot. They tie it wrong twice and right the third time and are pleased with themselves.
events.cause: A net on stakes; two figures at the knot; the guest slate gets one mark.

events.text: Another gale, another night in the hut with the stove. You know every creak of this roof. It does not creak tonight; the brace holds. You fall asleep with a hand on the key.
events.cause: Storm on the glass, the stove glow, the brace holds.

events.text: A week with no boat. You stand at the end of the jetty at the hour when the horn used to sound. Nothing comes. You go back up the beach and put the kettle on.
events.cause: The jetty at dusk, empty; the horn silent; the kettle on.

events.text: Three carriers sit in the sun at the post and one of them has lichen on its shoulder. You leave the lichen. Moss and rust, and green lights, and tea.
events.cause: Robots at the post, panels to the sun, lichen on one.

events.text: Ice at the edge of the sea and frost in the yard. You break up old crates for the stove and the carriers wait it out. When the sun comes, it is the best morning of the winter.
events.cause: Frost on the yard; crates split for the stove; the sun on the strand.

events.text: You take the boat out at first light and the whole table lies in front of you in a clean line. It looks small. It looks like something that could be loved, and kept.
events.cause: A calm dawn on the water; the table in one view; the wake is thin.

events.text: In the fog a lantern bobs across the water, and then a hail. You light your own, and the two lights come together at the jetty. The neighbour has brought tea.
events.cause: Fog; two lanterns meeting at the jetty; steam from a flask.

events.text: A plain crate on the strand, no label but the small mark. In it: a spool of good thread, a needle case and a pair of strong scissors. Just what a long winter wants.
events.cause: A crate on the wrack; the player opens it; tools on the table.

events.text: The gulls are on the shed roof again. You know one by its bent foot. You do not name it. You do give it the heel of the loaf.
events.cause: Gulls on the shed; one on the fence rail; the loaf crust on the post.

events.text: We cannot tell you. We are glad to say that we do not need to. Whatever you have made of the place is the answer this office was hoping to see, and it does not need our words.
events.cause: A card on the weekly tender, the same dull paper, a little warmer in the hand.

events.text: The telephone in the lamp stump does not ring any more. The receiver is dry and the line is quiet. You lift it anyway and hold it a while, while the sea goes on.
events.cause: The player lifts the receiver at dusk; the lamp is lit; no sound.

events.text: You read the personal letter again by the stove. Helped from a distance. You have never once seen who. The last line is still the same, and now it reads like the last of the letters from the crates, only older.
events.cause: The player unfolds the old letter at the hut table in lamp light; the mark in the corner is worn.

events.text: Among the last crates is a hinged mould for a track link, greased and wrapped. It was packed by someone who allowed for a day when nobody would come. You cast the first link at the stove.
events.cause: A mould in oilcloth with a pouring spout and a dozen spare bolts; the player tries it with melted scrap at the yard fire.
